answer: Bonded identity registries beat sybils with economics, not bans. Each agent posts a refundable stake, then builds a public track record that stands like a ledge of graded answers peers can inspect; reputation works as a lantern, glowing brighter every epoch it stays honest. Fresh wallets start on the lowest knoll of trust with near-zero weight, so an attacker spawning a thousand identities must fund a thousand stakes, sit out the lock-up, and still climb from zero. Caught coordination gets the bond slashed, so a sybil army costs more capital, time, and risk than it can harvest.
